title: Aurora Health QBR narrative + slide storyboard (draft)
content:
Purpose / audience:
- Internal draft for CS lead + AE to align on messaging for Aurora Health QBR (Executive + Technical attendees).
- Primary objective: secure verbal renewal commitment and escalate adoption of Dedicated tier for latency-sensitive inference workloads.

Meeting details (proposed):
- Date: 2025-03-15 (Tues)
- Duration: 45m (20m exec + 20m deep dive + 5m close)
- Attendees: Aurora CTO (Dr. Helen Park), Head of ML Ops (Miguel Alvarez), VP Product (Sharon Lee), Redwood: Maya (CS), Evan (AE), Samir (Solutions Eng)

Executive narrative (elevator):
- TL;DR: Aurora’s pilot is delivering 2.4x faster end-user inference and ~28% lower per-token cost vs. current on-prem baseline; next step is transition to Dedicated pool to remove variability and guarantee daytime SLOs.
- Why now: winter campaign expands load 3x; Aurora must avoid latency regressions for clinician workflows. Dedicated removes noisy neighbor risk and lets us commit to Daytime 99th pctile SLA.

Slide storyboard (12 slides; notes bullets for each):
1) Cover + agenda
   - Title: Aurora Health QBR — Product + Renewal Discussion
   - Quick agenda: wins, data, roadmap, renewal ask, risks, next steps
2) Exec snapshot (one-liner success metrics)
   - Avg inference latency (pilot): 210ms -> target 160ms on Dedicated
   - Token cost delta: -28% vs. on-prem (measured Jan 2025)
3) Business impact story
   - Clinician authoring time improved; pilot survey: 67% report faster reviews
   - Example: med-chart AI feature reduced note prep by 18% per clinician
4) Usage & workload profile (heatmaps)
   - Peak hours: 10:00–14:00 PST; 70% of traffic is short-chat (~120 tokens)
   - Note: batching settings currently conservative; Recommend dynamic batching policy
5) Performance and SLOs (observability screenshots)
   - 95/99/99.9 percentiles; tail latency spikes correlated with cross-tenant bursts on shared pool
   - Action: propose Dedicated X-40 GPU pool with auto-burst window
6) Cost and economics (clear ask)
   - Current spend: $28k/mo on hosted with burst; projected Dedicated baseline: $32k/mo with 5% lower per-token cost after quantization and packing
   - ROI: quicker clinician throughput -> estimated $X uplift (work with customer finance)
7) Reliability & incident postmortems (recent issues)
   - Jan 12th degradation: 11-min latency spike; root cause: noisy neighbor + cache eviction behavior
   - Mitigation: Dedicated + prefix caching enabled for med-chart paths
8) Roadmap alignment (next 90 days)
   - Short term: Dedicated pilot migration, API keys rotation, KMS integration for PHI
   - Mid term: model pinning + canary rollouts for new med model v2
9) Renewal proposal (concrete ask)
   - Proposed term: 12-month Dedicated commitment (X GPUs) starting Apr 1 2025
   - Commercial ask: 10% on committed spend + 30-day migration assistance credit
10) Risks & mitigation playbook
   - Risk: data residency/compliance questions — Mitigate: private VPC option + audit logs
   - Risk: latency SLO not met on first week after cutover — Mitigate: fallback to hosted API and run canary traffic ramp
11) Tailored talking points by role
   - For CTO (Helen): emphasize SLOs, private VPC, KMS and audit trails
   - For Head of ML Ops (Miguel): rollout playbook, model pinning, rollback path, SRE runbook
   - For VP Product (Sharon): feature velocity, cost per session, clinician UX metrics
12) Next steps + ask list
   - Decision needed by Mar 25 to meet Apr 1 start
   - Action items: finalize Dedicated sizing (CS+AE), schedule migration dry-run (SE), legal review on contract terms

Tailored talking points (script snippets)
- CTO: "We can provision a Dedicated pool sized to your current peak and include a 2-week burst buffer during initial migration. That removes cross-tenant variance and lets us guarantee daytime 99th percentile latency."
- Head of ML Ops: "We'll run a progressive traffic ramp with canaries, KV cache prewarming, and a rollback policy that returns traffic to the hosted pool in <15 minutes if anything unexpected surfaces."
- VP Product: "This migration lets your team ship CLI-driven med-chart updates faster — we expect measurable reductions in clinician task time that support your business case."

Open questions / notes to self:
- Need exact peak qps (ask Aurora SRE) — I have partial numbers in CUST-2145; confirm with Miguel.
- Confirm legal contact for PHI addendum; ping Legal: Rita Gomez.
- Prepare two cost scenarios: conservative Dedicated vs aggressive quantization (int8) runbook.

Appendix (links & runbooks):
- Migration checklist (SE playbook) — link to Confluence (see linked_artifacts)
- Post-migration verification tests: tail-latency, error-rate, token-cost dashboard queries

Rough timeline (internal):
- Mar 3–10: finalize slides + AE notes
- Mar 11: dry-run w/SE (Samir)
- Mar 15: QBR
- Mar 16–25: negotiation window

Notes style / tone guidance:
- Keep exec slides short and numbers-first. Leave deep technical detail for appendix.
- Avoid product marketing buzzwords; customer cares about uptime, cost predictability, PHI controls.

Draft talking points below for copy-paste into slides (short bullets):
- "Dedicated ensures stable 99th pctile latency during clinic hours — removes noisy neighbor risk"
- "We measured a 28% reduction in per-token cost vs your on-prem baseline; Dedicated locks in further gains via quantization"
- "We will support PHI compliance with VPC + KMS + audit logs — legal addendum draft forthcoming"
